title: Incident replay dashboard blueprint and trace conventions
content:
Goal:
Provide a pragmatic blueprint for building a dashboard and lightweight tracing conventions that enable fast incident "replay" for LLM inference regressions (latency/cost/quality), with low instrumentation overhead and explicit ownership. This is a working doc / playbook — iterate and prune.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: oncall SREs, serving runtime engineers, product owners running rollouts, and solutions engineers who debug customer regressions.
- Scope: dashboards intended to recreate the customer-visible "session story" using metrics + sampled traces + request payload fingerprints. Not an exhaustive list of all metrics. Focus on signals that help decide: cache vs compute vs model-quality root cause.

High-level outcomes (what success looks like):
- Operator can reproduce a problematic session timeline (0-5 mins) using a single dashboard and at most two trace links.
- Each dashboard panel has a clear owner and a short debugging intent string.
- Tracing naming and attributes are consistent enough to allow session-level aggregation across services and model variants.

Design principles / constraints:
- Low cost: default metric cardinality must be bounded; avoid per-prompt freeform tag explosion. Use hashed prompt-signature where necessary.
- Reproducibility: dashboard panels should use time-shifted queries and include a "replay anchor" widget (timestamp + request id).
- Fallthrough-friendly: widgets emphasize relative signals (percentiles, deltas) instead of absolute values.
- Ownership-first: every metric/widget line must map to an owner (team or person).

Metric definitions (compact):
- downstream.request.count
  - description: count of external API requests routed to inference.
  - unit: requests/sec (rate).
  - aggregation: sum over 1m.
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime
  - tags: endpoint, model_variant, customer_tier

- inference.latency.end_to_end
  - description: wall-clock time from HTTP accept to final write of response.
  - unit: ms
  - aggregation: p50/p90/p99 over 1m sliding window
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime
  - alert intuition: sustained p99 > 1200ms for >5m

- kvcache.hit_rate
  - description: ratio of key-value cache hits for generation requests
  - unit: percent
  - aggregation: 1m rate, cluster and tenant scopes
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime/cache
  - notes: sample cold start by tag cold_start=true

- tokens.billed_per_request
  - description: billed token count for each request (input+output)
  - unit: tokens
  - aggregation: median and 95th by endpoint/model_variant
  - owner: cost-ops

- model.fallback.count
  - description: times traffic was routed to fallback model variant (smaller/cheaper)
  - unit: count
  - aggregation: sum per 5m
  - owner: platform-routing

- generation.quality.regression_score
  - description: apply lightweight heuristics (BLEU-ish / hallucination heuristics) on sampled responses to detect step-changes in quality
  - unit: score (0-1)
  - aggregation: sample rate 0.5% by default, owner: applied-ml

Tracing conventions (short):
- Trace root: request span name = "req.<ingress>-to-serve" (e.g., req.api-gateway-to-serve)
- Per-stage child spans: e.g., "serve.kvcache.lookup", "serve.model.decode", "serve.routing.decision", "serve.postprocess.format"
- Span attributes (stable set):
  - inference.request_id (uuid)
  - model.variant (string)
  - tenant.id (hashed
  - sequence_length (int)
  - kvcache.hits (int)
  - batching.size (int)
  - cost.estimate_usd (float)
  - fallback.reason (string, optional)
- Naming heuristics: keep span names under 32 chars, lowercase, dots as separators. Avoid embedding freeform user or prompt text in span names; use hashed_prompt_sig attribute instead.

Span sampling guidance:
- Default: probabilistic sample 0.5% of requests across all traffic for full trace payloads.
- On-error: sample 100% of traces where inference.latency.end_to_end > p99 baseline OR generation.quality.regression_score drops below 0.6.
- Session capture: when a user session is flagged (synthetic probe failure or customer report), capture trace+request-body for up to 10 requests tied to that session id. Mark as replay=true.

Replay-oriented fields to capture (minimal):
- request_id, timestamp, model.variant, hashed_prompt_sig, prompt_length, response_length, kvcache.hits, route_decision_tag, error_code (if any), tenant.id_hash
- Store a compact JSON blob (max 2KB) attached to the trace for replay anchor containing: model variant, request_id, timestamp, small sanitized prompt signature, and pointer to stored request payload in secure bucket (if required).

Dashboard layout (single-page incident replay):
- Top row: "Anchor + quick facts"
  - widget: replay anchor (single value + copyable request_id) -> click opens trace and payload link
  - widget: small timeline sparkline of downstream.request.count (last 30m) with time-selector pinned to event window
  - widget: current p99 latency vs baseline (delta)
  - owner: eng-oncall

- Middle row: "Cause candidates" (3 panels)
  - kvcache heatmap: p50/p90 hit_rate by tenant cohort (small multiples)
    - viz: heatmap / small chart per cohort
    - query: kvcache.hit_rate grouped by tenant.cohort
    - owner: eng-serving-runtime/cache
  - batching artifact panel: batching.size distribution and correlation with latency (scatter)
    - owner: platform-engineering
  - model fallback spike: model.fallback.count and fallback.reason table
    - owner: platform-routing

- Bottom row: "Trace links + lightweight request details"
  - sampled traces table (3): p99-slowest traces near anchor time order, each row has link->trace viewer + request_id + model.variant + brief tags
  - request snapshots: small JSON widgets showing the sanitized prompt_signature and response length for the replay window
  - owner: eng-observability

Alerting & runbook ties:
- Each panel must include a one-line runbook hint: e.g., "If kvcache.hit_rate drop > 20% then check cache-population jobs (team: eng-serving-runtime/cache)."
- Create two compound alerts:
  1) inference-service-degradation: p99(latency) > baseline*1.4 AND kvcache.hit_rate decrease > 15% -> severity P1, page oncall
  2) model-fallback-surge: model.fallback.count > 50 in 5m for single region -> severity P2, notify routing owners

Investigative workflow (operator steps):
1) Open replay dashboard, click replay anchor (populates time window).
2) Inspect top cause candidates row. If kvcache looks low, click tenant cohort to open cohort drilldown.
3) Open the slowest sampled trace link and look for large "serve.model.decode" or long blocking "serve.kvcache.lookup" spans.
4) If no trace reveals issue, check batching.size scatter to surface correlation.
5) If quality regression suspected, check generation.quality.regression_score panel and open sampled responses. File a regression ticket with examples.

Instrumentation checklist (work-in-progress):
- [ ] Add hashed_prompt_sig attribute on ingress for all production routes (owner: dev-ex)
- [ ] Add sequence_length and batching.size attributes in model-serving runtime (owner: serving-runtime)
- [ ] Emit kvcache.hit/miss counters with tenant.cohort tag (owner: cache)
- [ ] Hook sampled response snapshots to secure S3 with TTL 30 days and attach pointer (owner: applied-ml)
- [ ] Add alert bindings for the two compound alerts (owner: observability)

Privacy & cost notes:
- Never store raw prompts in traces in prod. Use hashed_prompt_sig and, if needed, a sanitized redaction pipeline before storing any raw text in secure buckets.
- Sample rates must be configurable per-tenant; enterprise customers may request higher tracing for their traffic under NDA.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we surface multi-model fanout where a single request fans out to micro-models? Proposal: use span attribute fanout=true and have a mini-aggregate panel.
- Decide a stable list of tenant cohorts (prod, internal, trial) and hashing scheme.
- Spike: small PoC to replay 100 incidents from last quarter and time-to-diagnose measurement (owner: observability-ops).

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc short; migrate stable sections to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-OBS-REPLAY-001) after we validate with two incidents.
- Sync with Marco and Tara next week for sampling budget approval.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-REPLAY-001 (design doc)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-1298 (incident-replay backlog)
